source: Wikipedia (read 2026-11) Stanford Research Institute Problem Solver (STRIPS), summarising Fikes and Nilsson (1971)
finding: STRIPS (Fikes and Nilsson, SRI, 1971) defines an action by conditions that must hold, an add list and a delete list. Applying it gives (state minus deletes) plus adds. Everything not named stays unchanged. If preconditions fail the action has no effect.
numbers: Plan existence for propositional STRIPS is PSPACE-complete; some restricted forms are polynomial or NP-complete.
limits: Secondary source (encyclopedia), not the 1971 paper itself. Complexity result is Bylander 1994 (not opened).
agent_relevance: Gives the exact object O5 needs: a goal is a set of facts, each action is a (needs, adds, removes) triple, and working backwards means finding an action whose adds cover an open fact and then making its needs the new subgoals.

source: Valmeekam, Marquez, Sreedharan, Kambhampati (2023) On the Planning Abilities of Large Language Models: A Critical Investigation (NeurIPS 2023)
finding: LLMs asked to write full plans in classical IPC-style domains mostly fail. Best model GPT-4 averaged about 12% valid plans across domains.
numbers: Blocksworld zero-shot natural language GPT-4: 206/600 (34.3%) valid plans. Instruct-GPT3 far lower. Fine-tuned GPT-3 (1000 training instances) solved 122/600 (~20%). BLOOM one-shot: 4/250 (1.6%) Blocksworld, 0/50 mystery.
quote: only about 12% of the plans that the best LLM (GPT-4) generates are actually executable
limits: Single prompt style per cell; pre-reasoning-model era; small domains (Blocksworld, Logistics).
agent_relevance: A model that writes a whole plan in one shot cannot be trusted. Plans should be built and checked step by step by code.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) On the Planning Abilities of LLMs, name-obfuscation test
finding: Renaming actions and objects (Mystery Blocksworld, same logic, deceptive names) wipes out GPT-4 performance. This points to pattern matching on familiar words, not reasoning over preconditions and effects.
numbers: GPT-4 zero-shot natural language: 210/600 Blocksworld vs 1/600 Mystery Blocksworld vs 0/600 randomised names. PDDL-style prompts: 106 vs 3. Chain of thought did not help much over one-shot.
quote: whatever accidental planning performance LLMs show is likely connected to pattern matching rather than reasoning
limits: Obfuscation idea comes from IPC 1998 (McDermott) to test domain independence. Later o1-class models recover part of the loss (see b07).
agent_relevance: Test our O5 on obfuscated versions of tasks. If it only works with familiar names, it is not working backwards from effects.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) human baseline in On the Planning Abilities of LLMs
finding: Humans do far better than 2023 LLMs on the same Blocksworld instances and mostly find optimal plans.
numbers: 50 participants, one random instance each: 39 (78%) valid plan; 35 of those 39 (89.7%) optimal.
limits: One instance per person, with a worked example in the prompt; IRB study but not a controlled difficulty sweep.
agent_relevance: Sets the human bar: about 78% valid on tasks where GPT-4 got 34% zero-shot.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) LLM-Modulo settings: verifier back-prompting and LLM plans as seeds
finding: An external sound verifier (VAL) that returns the failing step fixes many LLM failures. Using the LLM plan as a seed for a local-search planner (LPG) cuts search steps in familiar domains but not in obfuscated ones.
numbers: Back-prompting up to 15 rounds on 50 previously failed instances per domain: Blocksworld 82% solved (avg 3.68 rounds), Logistics 70% (3.31 rounds), Mystery BW remained poor (about 10%, per b17). LPG search steps Blocksworld: 15.8 empty seed, 20.07 random seed, 14.5 GPT-4 seed. Edit distance about half of plan length.
limits: Back-prompting tested only on already failed instances, one model (GPT-4).
agent_relevance: Supports G2: revise from real checker output. Also shows the gain depends on the model producing a plausible first draft.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) user study of LLM-assisted human planning
finding: Giving humans GPT-4 plan suggestions did not improve their planning and led some to accept wrong plans.
numbers: 49 unassisted vs 48 LLM-assisted participants: no significant difference in accuracy, time or NASA-TLX load. 3 of 48 accepted incorrect LLM suggestions; 2 submitted them.
limits: Small groups; suggestions came from a weak 2023 model.
agent_relevance: Automation bias risk: a wrong draft plan can anchor the next step. A code check must stand between draft and acceptance.

source: Valmeekam, Stechly, Kambhampati (2024) LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs? A Preliminary Evaluation of OpenAI's o1 on PlanBench
finding: o1-preview is a large jump over earlier LLMs on 600-instance PlanBench Blocksworld, but not robust: it drops on obfuscation and on long plans, and is slow.
numbers: Blocksworld zero-shot: o1-preview 587/600 (97.8%), o1-mini 340/600 (56.6%), Fast Downward 600/600 in 0.265 s vs 40.4 s for o1-preview. Best old LLM LLaMA 3.1 405B 62.6% zero-shot. Mystery BW: o1-preview 41.6% zero-shot, 52.8% one-shot; Randomized Mystery 37.3%. Earlier LLMs on Mystery BW: 0 to 4.3%. Long plans (20 to 40 steps, 110 instances): o1-preview 23.63%.
limits: o1 reasoning traces hidden; possible training on PlanBench; cost opaque.
agent_relevance: Extended reasoning helps with preconditions and effects but degrades with plan length. A scaffold that checks each step addresses the length failure.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2024) o1 on PlanBench: unsolvable instances
finding: o1 mostly fails to say a problem is unsolvable. It tends to return an impossible plan or an empty plan.
numbers: Blocksworld unsolvable: 27% correctly flagged, 19% empty plan, 54% a full (invalid) plan. Randomized Mystery BW: 16% flagged, 5% empty plan, 79% full impossible plan. False claims of impossibility on solvable instances: 0% Blocksworld, 11.5% Randomized Mystery.
limits: Preliminary; one model family.
agent_relevance: A backward-chaining agent must detect a dead end (open goal with no achiever). Make that a code check, because the model cannot be trusted to say it.

source: Valmeekam, Stechly, Gundawar, Kambhampati (2024) Planning in Strawberry Fields: Evaluating and Improving the Planning and Scheduling Capabilities of LRM o1
finding: o1 beats LLMs on several planning and scheduling sets but is not close to a classical planner in cost or guarantees. Gains on obfuscated and PSPACE-hard (Sokoban) problems are small.
numbers: Logistics (200): 94%, randomized mystery 52%. Sokoban (55 instances, IPC 2008 generator): o1-preview 12.7%, o1-mini 10.9%, Llama3.1-405B 0%. TravelPlanner: o1-preview 10%, o1-mini 1.67%, previous direct-prompt best 4.4% (GPT-4-turbo). Graph colouring: o1-mini 96% vs 16% reported for GPT-4. Cost over 4000 USD for the study; per 100 instances o1-preview 42.12 USD vs GPT-4o-mini 0.02 USD.
limits: Authors argue for LLM-Modulo with a verifier; they have a stake in that view. Hidden reasoning tokens make cost uncontrolled.
agent_relevance: Shows where unaided long reasoning stops: state tracking plus search on hard domains. Argues for program-held state.

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) Chain of Thoughtlessness? An Analysis of CoT in Planning (NeurIPS 2024)
finding: Chain of thought helps on Blocksworld only when the demonstrated procedure matches the query class almost exactly. General algorithm prompts give small gains, and gains vanish as the stack grows beyond the demonstrated size.
numbers: Table-to-stack, 261 instances, GPT-4: zero-shot 3.83%, zero-shot CoT 4.98%, universal-algorithm CoT 51.3%, stacking-specific CoT 59.3%, progression-proof CoT 6.89%. GPT-4-Turbo: 19.1% zero-shot, 37.1% universal, 40.6% stacking. Claude-3-Opus: 9.96%, 37.1%, 24.5%. Self-consistency on these prompts lowered performance. Fast Downward 100% everywhere.
limits: Very simple problem class; 2024 models; also repeated on CoinFlip, LastLetterConcatenation and arithmetic variants.
agent_relevance: A written-out backward-chaining procedure only works as far as the examples go. Put the procedure in code (O5 as a program) and let the model fill only the slot.

source: Liu, Jiang, Zhang, Liu, Zhang, Biswas, Stone (2023) LLM+P: Empowering LLMs with Optimal Planning Proficiency
finding: Let the LLM only translate a task into a PDDL problem file and call a classical planner (Fast Downward). On 7 robot-planning domains LLM+P gives valid, mostly optimal plans where the LLM alone gives plans that break preconditions.
numbers: 7 domains (Barman, Blocksworld, Floortile, Grippers, Storage, Termes, Tyreworld), GPT-4, 200 s planner limit. Direct GPT-4 planning failed mainly on preconditions (cannot track ON and CLEAR in Blocksworld; does not clean glasses in Barman). Tree of Thoughts timed out in most cases. Exact table cells were garbled in the PDF text, so per-domain percentages are not recorded here.
limits: Needs a hand-written correct domain file and one example per domain. Failures were mainly in problem translation.
agent_relevance: The cleanest split of labour: the model translates, code plans. Fits our rule that the program decides and the model fills slots.

source: Silver, Dan, Srinivas, Tenenbaum, Kaelbling, Katz (2024) Generalized Planning in PDDL Domains with Pretrained LLMs (AAAI 2024)
finding: GPT-4 can write a Python program that solves unseen PDDL tasks, if it first summarises the domain, proposes a strategy, and debugs against training tasks. Results are all-or-nothing and strongly domain dependent.
numbers: Fraction of evaluation tasks solved (10 seeds, 30 tasks each): Delivery 0.90, Forest 1.00, Gripper 0.90, Miconic 0.01, Ferry 0.80, Spanner 0.10, Heavy 0.60. Ablation no debugging: 0.10, 0.62, 0.50, 0.00, 0.26, 0.00, 0.20. No CoT: 0.70, 1.00, 0.80, 0.13, 0.20, 0.00, 1.00. GPT-3.5 near 0 in most. Synthesised programs ran faster than Fast Downward LAMA.
limits: Used the ChatGPT browser interface with manual copy-paste. Mixed effect of CoT: helped 5, hurt Miconic and Heavy. Spanner fails because GPT-4 misses the one-way location chain.
agent_relevance: Automated debugging from real output was the biggest lever (e.g. Ferry 0.26 to 0.80). CoT strategy summary is not reliably helpful, so use it only on a signal.

source: Silver et al. (2024) error analysis for GPT-4 generalized planning
finding: Most failures are program errors the code can locate, not subtle plan flaws. Overfitting to the training tasks was rare.
numbers: Error types on training tasks, all runs: Python exception 40.0%, plan semantics 34.0%, plan syntax 13.0%, timeout 13.0%. In failed runs: exception 42.5%, semantics 31.4%. In successful runs: semantics 44.7%, exception 28.9%.
limits: Seven simple domains.
agent_relevance: Supports G2 and G3: give the model the exact failing output; check on held-out tasks.

source: Guan, Valmeekam, Sreedharan, Kambhampati (2023) Leveraging Pre-trained LLMs to Construct and Utilize World Models for Model-based Task Planning (NeurIPS 2023)
finding: GPT-4 writes PDDL action models (preconditions and effects) from text, humans or a validator fix them once, then a classical planner plans. This beats having the LLM plan.
numbers: GPT-4 produced PDDL for over 40 actions; 48 tasks (27 Household, 21 Logistics). Fast Downward with the corrected model: 95% Household, 100% Logistics. LLM planner alone (ReAct): 15% Household, 0% Logistics. LLM back-prompted by VAL using the LLM-acquired model: 48% and 33% (column order from garbled table; read with care). Failures of the planner route were only goal-translation errors.
limits: Fixed object types; needs human or validator correction of the domain model; only 3 domains.
agent_relevance: Writing the action model (preconditions and effects) is where the model is useful. Searching with it should be code.

source: Oswald, Srinivas, Kokel, Lee, Katz, Sohrabi (2024) Large Language Models as Planning Domain Generators (ICAPS 2024)
finding: Open models can write syntactically valid PDDL actions from text, but few are equivalent to the true domain. Bigger helps. Chat tuned models did worse than base models.
numbers: 9 domains; best model LLaMA-2-70b produced valid PDDL in 94% of cases and heuristically equivalent domains in 25%. Almost all syntax errors were unexpected-token errors; main semantic error was wrong predicate argument counts. Rewording descriptions (random or flipped predicate order) gave no consistent gain.
limits: Open models of 2023 only (LLaMA family, StarCoder); equivalence judged by a heuristic using plans from the K planner.
agent_relevance: Even effect lists the model writes need cross-checking by code. Do not trust a model-written effect list without running it.

source: Katz, Kokel, Srinivas, Sohrabi (2024) Thought of Search: Planning with Language Models Through the Lens of Efficiency (NeurIPS 2024)
finding: Search methods that call an LLM at each step (ToT, GoT, ReAct, RAP) are neither sound nor complete and cost thousands of calls. Having the LLM write only the successor and goal-test code, then running plain BFS or DFS, solves whole datasets exactly.
numbers: 24 game: 100% on all 1362 ToT instances, 1.92 to 6.83 s total, versus 75% for ToT on 100 medium problems with about 100 LLM calls each. Successor function needed 1.2 interactions on average (goal test 1). Mini crosswords and 502 BlocksWorld tasks also 100% accuracy; total run time around seconds. ToT call counts 12K to 482K versus a few.
limits: Needs a human or tests to catch wrong successor code; heuristic function left to future work.
agent_relevance: The successor function is exactly preconditions and effects. Model writes it once; program searches backward or forward. Strongest design hint for O5.

source: Kambhampati, Valmeekam, Guan, Verma, Stechly, Bhambri, Saldyt, Murthy (2024) Position: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks (ICML 2024)
finding: Position paper: LLMs are idea generators; sound critics must check. It restates Blocksworld numbers and extends the idea to TravelPlanner.
numbers: LLM-Modulo with VAL back-prompting: Blocksworld 82% in 15 rounds, Logistics 70%, Mystery BW about 10%. TravelPlanner: best prompt methods 0.7% for GPT-3.5-Turbo.
limits: Authors are advocates; the LLM-Modulo TravelPlanner results are cited from a separate preliminary report not opened here.
agent_relevance: Gives the rule: no plan accepted without an external sound critic. Matches G2 and G3.

source: Shojaee, Mirzadeh, Alizadeh, Horton, Bengio, Farajtabar (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: Reasoning models do better than standard models at medium puzzle complexity, equal at low, and all collapse to near zero beyond a complexity threshold, while thinking-token use falls near collapse. Blocks World is one of four puzzles.
numbers: Three regimes: standard models match or beat thinking models at low complexity; thinking models win at medium; both collapse at high. Models: o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet thinking. Blocks World with DeepSeek-R1: temperature zero collapses at N=4, sampling delays collapse to N=30.
limits: Exact-sequence scoring; challenged in b19. River Crossing and token-limit confounds.
agent_relevance: Planning quality drops sharply with size; scale the number of checked steps, not the length of free reasoning.

source: Opus and Lawsen (2025) The Illusion of the Illusion of Thinking (comment on Shojaee et al.)
finding: Rebuttal: part of the reported collapse is an evaluation artifact. Tower of Hanoi outputs exceed token limits, and River Crossing instances for N over 5 with boat capacity 3 have no solution but were scored as failures. Asking for a compact program restores high accuracy.
numbers: Tower of Hanoi 15 disks via a Lua function prompt: very high accuracy for Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude Opus 4, o3, Gemini 2.5, under 5000 tokens. No per-model percentage given in the short comment.
limits: Preliminary, a short comment, not on Blocks World; no full tables. Co-author is an AI model.
agent_relevance: Let the model emit a procedure and let code run it. Always check that a task is solvable before scoring a miss.

source: Verma, La, Favier, Mishra, Shah (2025) Teaching LLMs to Plan: Logical Chain-of-Thought Instruction Tuning for Symbolic Planning (PDDL-Instruct)
finding: Fine-tuning on explicit step reasoning about precondition satisfaction and effect application, with VAL feedback, raises valid-plan rate sharply but not to 100%.
numbers: Llama-3 with detailed feedback and 15 iterations: Blocksworld 94%, Mystery BW 64% (from 1% baseline), Logistics 79%. GPT-4 (limited access): 91%, 59%, 78%; GPT-4 baseline Blocksworld 28%, Mystery BW 1%, Logistics 11%. Average gain 66% (SD 3) over baseline for Llama-3 and 35% (SD 20) over plain instruction tuning.
limits: Training-based, so not a scaffold-only result. Test domains match PlanBench so contamination is possible; authors state it falls short of 100%. Single preprint.
agent_relevance: Shows that explicit checking of each action's preconditions and effects is what raises validity. We can get part of that by making code do the checks.

source: Cross-study synthesis of b02, b07, b16, b20 on Mystery Blocksworld
finding: Across 2023 to 2025 the same obfuscated task is the best discriminator between pattern matching and rule following. Scaffolds that run the rules (planner, verifier, fine-tuned logic chain) hold up; free text does not.
numbers: GPT-4 zero-shot: 0.17% (1/600). GPT-4 one-shot: 4.3% (26/600) per b07 table. o1-preview zero-shot 41.6%. Llama-3 fine-tuned with PDDL-Instruct 64%. Fast Downward 100%.
limits: Different test samples and prompt formats between papers; no single controlled comparison.
agent_relevance: Use obfuscated tasks as our own O5 test. A pass there means real backward use of preconditions.

source: Cross-study synthesis: failed or fragile effects in planning with LLMs
finding: Four moderators recur. (1) Plan length: gains vanish for long plans. (2) Name familiarity: gains vanish under obfuscation. (3) Prompt specificity: CoT helps only if matched to the problem class. (4) An external verifier returns a large share of the loss.
numbers: o1-preview: 97.8% overall vs 23.63% on 20 to 40 step plans (b07). CoT: 3.83% to 59.3% only with a stacking-specific prompt (b10). Back-prompting: 82% Blocksworld in 15 rounds (b05). Obfuscation: 210/600 to 1/600 (b03).
limits: Synthesis across papers with different models; most results come from one research group (Arizona State), so independent replication is thin.
agent_relevance: Design for these four: short checked steps, no reliance on names, procedure in code, verifier in the loop.

source: Independence check on the evidence base (this subfield)
finding: Independent groups reach the same direction. Silver et al. (MIT/IBM), Katz et al. (IBM), Liu et al. (UT Austin) and Verma et al. (MIT) agree that LLM alone is weak and LLM plus program or planner is strong. Only the Arizona State group reports the obfuscation and CoT-specificity results; no independent replication of those two was found in the sources opened.
numbers: Silver et al: GPT-4 + debugging solved 0.80 to 1.00 in 4 of 7 domains; Liu et al: classical planner after LLM translation; Katz et al: 100% with LLM-written successor code.
limits: No search of failed replications beyond the b19 comment was possible (web search budget was used up). Gap noted.
agent_relevance: Treat the plan-with-checker claim as well supported; treat obfuscation and CoT-specificity as single-group findings until replicated.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2022) PlanBench: An Extensible Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Planning and Reasoning about Change
finding: Eight test types on Blocksworld and Logistics. Even GPT-4 is weak at plan generation; it does better on easier sub-skills such as replanning and goal reformulation.
numbers: GPT-4 vs Instruct-GPT3 (text-davinci-002), Blocksworld, 600 instances: plan generation 206 (34.3%) vs 41 (6.8%); cost-optimal 198 (33%) vs 35 (5.8%); plan verification 191 (31.8%) vs 4 (0.6%); execution reasoning 141/500 (28.2%) vs 49/500 (9.8%); replanning 461 (76.8%) vs 467 (77.8%); plan generalization 348 vs 363 of 600.
quote: LLMs are pretty ineffective in reasoning about actions and change
limits: Table rows blur in PDF text; only some rows recorded with confidence. Replanning is easy because the original plan is shown.
agent_relevance: Plan verification by the model was weak (31.8%), so verify with code (G1, G2).

source: Valmeekam et al. (2022) PlanBench: auxiliary tasks show where the failure sits
finding: Reasoning about plan execution (applying actions to a state) is a weak spot for GPT-4. This is the basic precondition-effect skill that backward and forward planning both use.
numbers: Plan execution reasoning: GPT-4 141/500 (28.2%), Instruct-GPT3 49/500 (9.8%). Plan verification: GPT-4 191/600 (31.8%).
limits: Few-shot prompts with a single worked example; 2022 models.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on the model to simulate action effects. Let code apply the add and delete lists.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) relaxed-plan assessment of GPT-4 plans
finding: Even with delete and precondition relaxations, many GPT-4 Blocksworld plans still fail to reach the goal, so errors are not only small precondition slips.
numbers: Under the most lenient mode (delete plus precondition relaxed) 39% of plans were still incorrect across prompt configurations.
limits: Figure-level numbers read from text; prompt configs pooled.
agent_relevance: Goal reaching itself fails, not only action legality. Check goals with code at the end of each backward chain.

source: Thought of Search (Katz et al. 2024) complexity audit of LLM search methods
finding: Table of published LLM-search methods: none is both sound and complete; cost per instance is large. Abandoning soundness gave no efficiency benefit.
numbers: ToT on four tasks: 3.3% of states considered with 245K calls on one task, 388% with 482K on another; GoT and others up to 1.44M calls on one dataset; ReAct and ReWOO much cheaper but with weaker accuracy.
limits: Table layout garbled in PDF text; figures are read approximately.
agent_relevance: Per-step model judgement over a tree is expensive and unsound; keep tree search in the program.

source: Chain of Thoughtlessness: synthetic scalable domains
finding: The same failure pattern appears outside Blocksworld: CoT gains on CoinFlip, LastLetterConcatenation and multi-digit arithmetic variants fall as problem size grows past the demonstrated size.
numbers: Tested GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Llama3-70b, Llama3-8b on arithmetic across temperatures; accuracy plummets with length while syntactic properties may generalise. Exact curve values are in figures, not recorded here.
limits: Figure values not read; text claims only.
agent_relevance: Procedure demos teach pattern copying. Do not put a long worked backward-chain demo in the prompt and call it a method.
